title: Sell Mineral Rights in Laurel, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Laurel, MT
metaDescription: Laurel, MT is a refining town, not a producing field — the crude runs through, it isn't pulled from under it. I buy mineral interests near Laurel directly.
heroLead: People hear Laurel and assume the refinery means the ground under it is producing. Usually it isn't — the crude just passes through.
intro: I get this question from Laurel families more than almost anywhere else in the state: does the refinery mean my family's minerals are worth something? Almost always the answer is no, at least not for that reason. The refinery in Laurel processes crude shipped in by pipeline and rail — Canadian, Bakken, some regional — it doesn't run on wells drilled under the town. If you own minerals near Laurel, their value depends on whether there's actual conventional exploration or production history under your specific parcel, which in this stretch of Yellowstone County has been limited.

What I do see a lot of around Laurel is mineral severance tied to the town's railroad and industrial development history. When the Northern Pacific built through here and the refinery and rail yards went in over the following decades, plenty of farmland got subdivided and sold off in pieces, with mineral rights reserved separately from the surface more often than families expect.

sections.heading: What's actually under Laurel-area ground
paragraphs: There's some scattered stripper production and older conventional wells in the county, but nothing tied specifically to the refinery's operation. I evaluate a Laurel interest the same way I'd evaluate any Yellowstone County parcel — production history, lease status, proximity to any active unit — not by assuming refinery activity translates to drilling activity, because it usually doesn't.

sections.heading: Subdivided land and severed minerals
paragraphs: If your family sold or subdivided land near Laurel decades ago and kept the mineral rights, that's a common pattern here, and it means your interest can outlive the original property by generations, attached to ground you may never have set foot on. I trace that chain through the Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder in Billings.

faqs.question: Does the refinery mean my minerals near Laurel are valuable?
faqs.answer: Not directly. The refinery processes crude shipped in from elsewhere rather than crude produced locally. I evaluate your interest based on actual drilling and lease history on your parcel.

faqs.question: My family sold the land but kept the minerals — is that unusual?
faqs.answer: Not around Laurel. It's a common pattern from the town's industrial development era, and I trace those severed interests through the county records.

faqs.question: Is there any active drilling near Laurel right now?
faqs.answer: Limited. I check your specific section for lease status and recent permits before discussing value.
